dataProvenance: synthetic deterministic fixtures; no AWS calls
limitations: Fixtures are not field measurements or evidence of environmental savings.
No realised-weight replay is reported; expected kilograms are not ground truth.
The insertion and 2-opt heuristics do not prove global optimality.

metricDefinitions.comparison: distance comparison only when expected kg tie; otherwise TRADE_OFF
metricDefinitions.expectedCollectionKg: sum of P0 confirmedKg * readinessPrior for selected stops
metricDefinitions.expectedKgPerKm: expectedCollectionKg / totalKm, null if totalKm is zero
metricDefinitions.reservedLoadKg: sum of full-load reservations including capacity buffer
metricDefinitions.totalKm: sum of directed fixture-matrix legs including depot return
metricDefinitions.totalMin: travel, waiting and service from shift start through depot return

results.description: All suppliers ready; both tie on expected kg and km, with different stable route orders.
A NOT_READY cancellation stays visible and is not routed.
No READY confirmation produces an explicit empty route and target gap.
A distant small mandatory supplier is served before optional target choices.
Full reservations, not probability-weighted kg, block the third stop.
A 2000 kg mandatory confirmation cannot fit a 2000 kg truck with buffer.
Arrival before window end is insufficient when service finishes late.
The stop is reachable but depot return exceeds shift end.
A missing directed return leg remains infeasible rather than zero cost.
Zero-distance insertions use a bounded denominator and stable ID tie.
All feasible supply is selected and the actual expected target gap remains.
Every optional stop violates its service window.
A READY cold-start supplier is usable with disclosed P0 assumptions.
All three stops needed; nearest-first chooses a longer directed order.
An efficient first choice can prevent a larger two-stop load; no universal kg winner.
Hazards, unsupported material and outbound radius apply to both planners.
Wait for opening, finish exactly at closing, and return exactly at shift end.
A zero optional target never suppresses a promised pickup.
